patches.summary: Replace defer rows.Close() with explicit Close() after iteration in novel commands.
patches.reason: SQLite MaxOpenConns=2; defer inside a for-mailboxes loop defers to function return, not loop end. Inner queries need a connection from the same pool, causing deadlock when both connections are held by deferred closes.
patches.validated_outcome: Greptile review 5/5 on PR #806 after fix.

patches.summary: Use upgraded_at timestamp from API response instead of synced_at for last upgrade time.
patches.reason: synced_at reflects when the record was cached locally, not when the trust upgrade actually occurred. The API returns upgraded_at in the response data.

patches.summary: Add mailboxes_id to test items in TestUpsertBatch_SetsMailboxesEmailsParentID.
patches.reason: The mailboxes_emails typed table has a NOT NULL constraint on mailboxes_id. Test items without it cause the typed upsert to fail, falling through to generic resources only.

patches.summary: Average two middle elements for even-length latency slices in median calculation.
patches.reason: Integer division picks the upper-middle element for even-length sorted slices (e.g. [1,2,3,4] returns 3 instead of 2.5), consistently skewing median_latency upward.

patches.summary: Parse $.recipients JSON array and use AND-logic: a send is covered only when ALL recipients match allowlist patterns.
patches.reason: json_extract returns the raw JSON array string for $.recipients. The string never matches any pattern. After expanding the array, OR-logic (any match = covered) overstates coverage for mixed-recipient sends — a single unallowed recipient gates the entire send.

patches.summary: Derive median_latency from audit-log decision events joined with oversight items instead of querying only the oversight table.
patches.reason: Sync maps oversight to /v1/oversight/pending, so decided items leave that endpoint and the local DB never has status != 'pending'. The original query filtered status != 'pending' → always zero rows → always '—'. The fix joins audit-log approve/reject events (decision timestamp) with oversight items (received_at) via resource_id.

patches.summary: Apply --days cutoff filter to pending_count for consistency with windowed decision counts.
patches.reason: total_decisions, approved, and rejected are filtered by --days window but pending_count was unwindowed, making the row metrics inconsistent when comparing volumes across the same time window.

patches.summary: Add allowlist as a dependent sync resource so allowlist coverage has data after sync --full.
patches.reason: The allowlist table was defined in the schema but never populated by sync. GET /v1/mailboxes/{mailboxId}/allowlist exists in the API.

patches.summary: Derive thread data from mailboxes_emails thread_id groups when the threads table is empty.
patches.reason: The API has no list-threads endpoint (only GET single thread by ID), so sync --full cannot populate the threads table. The command now falls back to grouping emails by $.thread_id from the API response.

patches.summary: Derive reply_rate from mailboxes_emails outbound emails with $.thread_id instead of the reply table.
patches.reason: The reply endpoint is POST-only (no list GET), so sync cannot populate the reply table. Outbound emails with a thread_id are replies to existing conversations.

patches.summary: Derive thread_count and avg_thread_depth from mailboxes_emails $.thread_id groups instead of the threads table.
patches.reason: The API has no list-threads endpoint (only GET single thread by ID), so sync --full cannot populate the threads table. Thread metrics are now derived from $.thread_id grouping with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2.

patches.summary: Derive upgrade_count and last_upgrade_at from audit-log events instead of the upgrade table. Excludes request/pending actions to count only completed upgrades.
patches.reason: The upgrade endpoint is POST-only (no list GET), so sync cannot populate the upgrade table. Audit-log entries with completed upgrade actions provide the same data. LIKE '%upgrade%' alone would match request_upgrade/upgrade_pending events, inflating the count.

patches.summary: Derive recent_sends from mailboxes_emails outbound emails instead of the send table.
patches.reason: The send endpoint is POST-only (no list GET), so sync cannot populate the send table. Outbound emails from mailboxes_emails provide a richer and syncable data source for coverage analysis.

patches.summary: Use event timestamps ($.created_at, $.received_at) instead of synced_at for --days window filtering.
patches.reason: synced_at is when the record was cached locally. On first-time sync, all historical records land with synced_at ≈ now, making --days 7 include all history. Using the actual event timestamp produces correct windowed results regardless of sync timing.

patches.summary: Check $.mailbox_id and $.metadata.mailbox_id for audit-log mailbox association.
patches.reason: The audit-log schema may store mailbox association in $.mailbox_id or $.metadata.mailbox_id. oversight_velocity was only checking $.mailbox_id, risking zero results if the field is stored in metadata.

patches.summary: Add $.mailbox_id check to trust_status audit-log query for consistency with oversight_velocity.
patches.reason: trust_status checked only $.metadata.mailbox_id but not $.mailbox_id. If upgrade events store mailbox association at the top level, trust_status would return zero upgrade_count and fall back to creation time for time_at_level.

patches.summary: Set isList=true in resolveRead call so local-store fallback uses db.List() instead of extracting 'pending' as a resource ID.
patches.reason: isList=false causes resolveLocal to split the path /v1/oversight/pending and call db.Get('oversight', 'pending'), which always returns not-found. --data-source local and auto-mode offline fallback were broken.

patches.summary: Use start-anchored LIKE patterns ('approve%', 'reject%') instead of '%approve%' / '%reject%' in both count and latency queries.
patches.reason: Unanchored '%approve%' matches negation prefixes like 'unapprove' or 'pre_approval_check', silently inflating approval/rejection counts and skewing approval_rate.

patches.summary: Remove $.resource_id = mb.ID from audit-log mailbox association queries. resource_id stores the target object ID (oversight item, upgrade object), not the mailbox ID.
patches.reason: The $.resource_id arm never matches a mailbox ID, making it dead code. Leaving it suggests resource_id is a mailbox field, which could mislead future queries.

patches.summary: Guard parent_id injection in syncDependentResource so API-provided values are preserved.
patches.reason: Unconditional obj["parent_id"] = parentIDJSON overwrites API thread-parent data with the mailbox UUID. The mailboxes_id FK injection was already guarded; parent_id was not.

patches.summary: Use json_extract(data, '$.thread_id') from the API response for thread grouping and reply detection instead of the parent_id column.
patches.reason: The parent_id column in mailboxes_emails is the FK to the parent mailbox, not a thread-parent reference. The API returns thread_id in EmailSummary. Using parent_id caused reply_rate to equal outbound rate and thread_count to collapse to 1 per mailbox.
